clips.title: [Tutorial] - How to use GitHub REST API for Beginners
clips.why: A quick first look at GitHub's REST API: a URL, a token, and JSON back.
look: Every resource has a URL, such as a repo or its pull requests.
The answer is JSON with the same field names Octokit gives you.
Without a token you can read public data, with a low limit.
clips.after: Octokit wraps exactly these URLs in one typed method each, so octokit.rest.pulls.get is this call without the string building.

clips.title: GitHub Automation with Octokit (with Gregor Martynus) — Learn With Jason
clips.why: The maintainer of Octokit sets up a client from scratch and explains how it is put together.
look: Creating one client with a token.
How methods are grouped by area of the API.
Why the client adds the headers and the API version for you.
clips.after: The independent-approval check and the metrics job create one client like this, with the job's token or the App's token.

clips.title: API Pagination: Making Billions of Products Scrolling Possible
clips.why: A clear picture of why APIs return lists in pages, and the two common ways to ask for the next one.
look: Offset pagination, which GitHub's REST API uses with page and per_page.
Cursor pagination, which GitHub's GraphQL API uses with endCursor.
Why one call never gives you the whole list.
clips.after: octokit.paginate follows GitHub's next-page links for you, which is what the story's first check forgot to do.

practice.q: Finish the line so it returns every commit of the PR, however many pages there are.
practice.hint: The Octokit helper that follows the next-page links.
practice.why: paginate takes the method itself and follows every page, so the 31st commit is never lost.

practice.q: Which of these calls is a bug waiting for a long PR?

options.why: pulls.get returns one object, not a list, so there is no page two.
It returns only the first page of reviews. A PR with many review rounds can hide the newest decision on page two.
This already pages through every file.

practice.q: Finish the filter that keeps only approvals for the code that would be merged now.
practice.hint: The newest commit of the PR's branch.
practice.why: An approval on an older commit approved code that is no longer the PR's head.

practice.q: Put the steps of the independent-approval check's main() in order.
items: Create one Octokit client with the job's token
Read the PR with pulls.get and keep head.sha
Page through all commits and reviews with paginate
Keep approvals from people on the head commit, outside the set of requesters and pushers
Set the exit code: 0 if one independent approval is left, 1 if none
practice.why: The head SHA comes first because every later comparison needs it, and the lists must be complete before anything is decided.

practice.q: Why does an agent's draft PR body end with Requested-by: @sean?

options.text: GitHub requires a trailer on draft PRs
options.why: GitHub has no such rule. The line is our own contract.

options.text: The PR's author is the bot, so the check needs the line to know which person asked for the work
options.why: The check adds that person to the requesters, who can never be the one approval.

options.text: So that GitHub requests Sean as a reviewer
options.why: The opposite: the requester is the one person whose approval does not count.
